doc.title: Bill Allred interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 24, 2017

title: Manassas Jazz Festival and meeting Wild Bill Davison
summary: Kincaid gets him onto the Manassas festival where he meets Davison, Lou McGarrity, Cutty Cutshall and Wallace Davenport; he thanks Kincaid in hospital.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: I’m not familiar with him I’m sorry to say.

Oh what an unbelievable player. But anyway he said, “I like the way you play,” he said, “you know” he says, “I go to this Manassas Jazz Festival up by Washington, DC” and he said, “God all the musicians, I think I could get you on that.” I said, “Well I don’t have any cred to help you.” And he said, “No yeah I can do it.” So by God he got me on that festival. And I met Wild Bill Davison, who I later toured with, Lou McGarrity, Cutty Cutshall, Eddie Con — I mean all the guys. And I got to play with them. I mean Jesus I got —
Pinch me, right? I can’t believe this, alongside with those people.

I know. I mean you know so I told Dean, when he asked me, and if anybody asks me, I’d played like the Mississippi Jazz Festival or something back home, but nobody there. So I got to meet these guys and a lot of Washington, DC players as well that I’ve remained

friends with for years. But I’m thinking God dang this is unbelievable. And it was. I mean Lou McGarrity. And I met Wallace Davenport, a black trumpeter who was pretty hot in New Orleans, and ended up doing two albums with him and would go down to New Orleans and sit in with him. You know I couldn’t sign on because he was on a small club group. But that was the biggest door that anybody had ever opened for me. Well later on Dean was sick and he was in the hospital here in Orlando. And he was terminal, the word was. And I went up to the hospital hat in hand and I said, “Dean, man, I’m sorry you are ill.” I said, “But I’ve got to tell you, you put me on the map, you made it for me.” He said, “Awww you would have done it by yourself.” I said, “No you’re wrong. I wouldn’t have. I could never have gone anywhere and met the volume of people.” And I said, “Jesus.” And then later on, the first thing Wild Bill Davison ever said to me, he was getting ready to do a set. And they had me scheduled with some sets. And I went up to him and I said, “Wild Bill” I said, “I’ve kind of been a fan of yours forever” you know, “I love what you do and then the Condon thing.” And I said, “Can I do a set with you sometime.” And of course Wild Bill of course, the old bastard, he said “You want to play with me” he said, “I’ve got a set coming up” he said, “get your ass up on the bandstand and let’s have some fun.” So I gave it my best shot and later he hired me for all kinds of stuff overseas.
